narrative:
The model estimates an 84% chance that you will leave your job, which is why your promotion request has been denied. This high probability reflects patterns the system sees in your profile that historically align with employees who end up departing.

Three factors stood out most in the decision. First, having received other job opportunities while at your current company was the strongest influence, pushing the prediction strongly toward leaving. Employees predicted to stay rarely report outside offers, so this signal carried significant weight. Second, your overall career experience of 6–10 years also pulled the prediction toward departure. While this range is fairly common among those expected to stay (about 35%), the model sees it as increasing turnover risk compared with shorter tenures. Third, working in the “other” sector rather than medical or education contributed noticeably toward leaving. Only about 22% of employees predicted to stay work in this broader category, making it a relevant differentiator.

Taken together, these elements outweighed positive factors such as your medical coverage, recognition you receive, and sense of job stability. The organization should review whether your external opportunities and sector-specific challenges can be addressed through targeted retention measures. You may wish to discuss how your experience and aspirations align with long-term roles here, helping reduce the risk the model has identified. (218 words)
